answer: One operator wearing many masks shares one inference pipeline, so gate on throughput, not keys. Each epoch the node fires simultaneous, tight-deadline skill challenges, and every identity must dock its own fresh answer at the submission wharf inside one narrow window. A lone backend driving fifty masks runs them serially and misses the signal, while graders cross-check each reply against an atlas of that account's past latency to catch masks answering in lockstep. Faking N live responders means buying N independent compute stacks, so attacker cost scales with real hardware, not cheap aliases.
